Some of it is legit, some are just memes. Generally a companion plant should share all or one of these factors;

  • protects against a disease/fungus/pest.
  • has similar growing requirements.
  • protects plant with shade or supports it (like beans and corn).
  • can be harvested at different times. Like lettuce, onions, and carrots interplanted.

Corn is greedy - plant it apart from everything else or it will suck up all the water and nutrients from the soil, and your other plants won't be as large.

Beyond that, all I've really learned about plants is to pay attention to your sunlight - I like to plant the garden from north to south, tallest plants at the north end and shortest plants at the south end, so that there will be no short plants hiding in the shadow of the tall ones, not getting enough sunlight.
